title: Mitigate GPU page-backpressure causing tenant session starvation and cache-stitch corruption
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reported correlated GPU OOM cascades over the last 10 days. Root cause analysis indicates a previously-unseen interaction: an allocator-level page-backpressure path pins tensor pages under heavy simultaneous KV cache eviction and long-lived session checkpoints. The pinning prevents slab reclamation, causing escalating fragmentation and eventual OOMs. A separate race in our KV cache "stitch" path allowed stale handle handoff during eviction, producing memory corruption that accelerated fragmentation. This ticket tracks a targeted runtime patch that introduces: (1) a conservative page-unwind/backpressure smoothing routine, (2) epoch-based KV-handle invalidation to avoid stale handoffs, and (3) a background compaction/eviction shunt for high-pressure tenants.
work_notes: 2025-02-18: Triage call with SRE, Support, and Runtime. Customers: two hosted startups and one enterprise Dedicated customer. Initial mitigation: increased per-tenant soft memory limit and enabled model-variant fallback for heavy tails (manual, temporary).

2025-02-19: Reproduction steps captured by eng on a dedicated repro harness (gpu-memstorm). Repro shows repeated small allocations + KV churn triggers page pin spikes on Turing-series nodes. Recorded heap/arena snapshots and a flamegraph of allocator activity. Link: https://dashboards.redwood.dev/d/runtime/gpu-memstorm

2025-02-20: Root cause hypothesis: allocator marks pages busy during async DMA/transfer; concurrent KV eviction mis-handles pointer lifetimes in cache-stitch. Confirmed via ASAN/memcheck runs on repro. Created PoC patch for handle epoch checks and a slow-path that forces KV-stitch to re-validate pointers before reuse.

2025-02-21: Implemented page-unwind throttle (configurable) to allow slab compaction cycles to complete before admitting new heavyweight allocations. Added metric gpu.page_unwind_throttle and gauge to measure throttle duration.

2025-02-22: Created PR that combines both fixes and unit + integration tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821. PR includes new stress test harness test/tensors/pagebackpressure_test.cc and a feature flag 'page_unwind_v2' guarded by runtime config.

2025-02-23: QA ran canary on a small fleet of dedicated nodes (3 nodes) and a hosted canary cluster for 48h. Observed no OOMs and a 60% reduction in page-pin spikes. Memory fragmentation metric slab.fragment_ratio dropped from 0.42 to 0.17 in canary. Logged canary dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.dev/d/canary/page-unwind-v2

2025-02-24: Customer communication: support team notified impacted customers of planned restart window and rollback plan. Temporary mitigation documented: 'force-kv-evict-tenant' admin tool and per-tenant throttle increase. Confluence incident runbook updated: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Runtime+Pagebackpressure+Investigation

2025-02-25: Rollout started to Dedicated (staged 10% -> 50%). Observed two brief model-quality regressions in heavy batching workloads; root cause: background compaction causing slight latency spikes under extreme QPS. Tuned compaction backoff to favor latency for hosted tier.
acceptance_criteria: No repeat OOMs or allocator panics in staged fleet for 7 days
KV cache-stitch race eliminated: no ASAN/memcheck violations in repro harness
Fragmentation metrics (slab.fragment_ratio) improve >30% in canary vs baseline
Automated regression test added to CI that replicates the eviction/handoff pattern
Rollout plan and rollback documented with clear metrics thresholds
postmortem_actions: Add long-running heap/fragmentation heatmap to Console per-tenant view
Introduce configurable tenant-level emergency-evict API for SRE/support
Follow-up: evaluate moving KV cache to handle-refs with hazard pointers or refcount epochs (RFC in progress)
Schedule a blue-team review to validate allocator invariants under future kernel/driver upgrades
notes_for_release: Feature gated behind 'page_unwind_v2' and default-enabled for Dedicated and Private in runtime-1.28. For Hosted, rollout gradually with latency-safe compaction thresholds. Ops: monitor gpu.page_unwind_throttle and slab.fragment_ratio; rollback by disabling feature flag and reverting PR 4821 if we see regressions.
customer_updates: 2025-02-20: Initial acknowledgement to customers and ETA for investigation: 72 hours
2025-02-24: Notification of pending patch and scheduled restart window (2025-02-26 02:00-04:00 UTC)
2025-02-26: Post-deploy note: patch applied, observed reduction in OOM rate; SRE continuing observation and will provide 7-day follow-up
